_note: What each number in the code means, with the evidence and the kind of claim it is -- read off the code, derived from something read, or guessed. A number may have several meanings and they are all listed: 0x320 is the player's collision radius and also the byte stride of a row of the terrain grid. tools/consts.py reads this and cross-references every site in all four executables. A meaning with a `routines` list holds only inside those routines; elsewhere the number is shown as a cross-reference and not as a claim about that site.

meanings.name: CELL
meanings.where: game:0x80033b8c grid_cell_at, and everywhere a world coordinate is formed
meanings.evidence: World X and Z are 2048 units to the grid cell: actor_stand_at_home forms x = cell_x << 11 + fine x. FORMATS.md, 'World X/Z = 2048 x cell'.

meanings.name: FIXED_ONE
meanings.where: game:0x800448b8 and every GTE matrix build
meanings.evidence: The fixed point this game multiplies in: `mult` then `sra` by 12, so 0x1000 is 1.0. An object record is initialised with 0x1000 in its three scale fields (+0x2c, +0x2e, +0x30), and a TMD's scale word is the same.

meanings.name: PLAYER_RADIUS
meanings.evidence: The radius literal the player's movement passes to the collision: `li $a3, 0x320` immediately before `jal collide_surface`. FORMATS.md, 'radius 0x320, body height 0x6a4 and collision flags 0x31 are literals in the routine'.

meanings.name: GRID_ROW_BYTES
meanings.evidence: The same number, unrelated: a terrain cell is at grid + cz*800 + cx*10, so a row of 80 cells of 10 bytes is 800 bytes. Confirmed from the code after first being guessed -- FORMATS.md, 'Two constants confirmed from the code'.

meanings.name: GRID_CELL_BYTES
meanings.evidence: Ten bytes to a terrain cell, from the same index arithmetic.

meanings.name: GRID_SIDE
meanings.evidence: The grid is 80 by 80 and grid_query_area bounds both axes by it.

meanings.name: PLAYER_HEIGHT
meanings.evidence: The body height literal in the player's movement, passed to the collision beside the radius.

meanings.name: PLAYER_COLLIDE_FLAGS
meanings.evidence: The collision flag word the player's movement asks for. Only the sites inside the movement routines are this; 0x31 is also just 49.

meanings.name: OBJECT_STRIDE
meanings.evidence: 68 bytes to an object record. Every walk of the object table steps by it -- `$s2 += 0x44` -- and find_object forms object_table + a0 * 0x44.

meanings.name: OBJECT_COUNT
meanings.evidence: 396 object records, the bound on every index into the table at 0x80191a5c: `slti $v0, $a0, 0x18c`.

meanings.name: ACTOR_STRIDE
meanings.evidence: 136 bytes to a creature record in the table at 0x80185da8.

meanings.name: ACTOR_COUNT
meanings.evidence: 199 creature slots: the teardown at level load passes over exactly that many entries of the 0x88 table.

meanings.name: FLAG_MASK
meanings.evidence: flag_gate masks the gate byte with 0x7f, which is why the flag array is 128 long and not 64.

meanings.name: VSTEP_PLACE
meanings.evidence: Inside 0x80 of the surface the player is *placed* on it rather than eased towards it, and 0x80 is also the largest single step towards it. tools/movement.py reproduces 48 of 48 of the game's height stores with it.

meanings.name: VSTEP_FALL
meanings.evidence: A gap wider than 0x400 stops being a step and becomes a fall: below the surface by more than this enters state 0x40, above it enters state 0x20.

meanings.name: OBJECT_OPCODES
meanings.evidence: 236 arms in the object interpreter's switch, stated by the guard `sltiu $v0, $v1, 0xec` on the opcode byte at object-1... the byte at -0x4 of the walking pointer. Read by tools/rdis.py, which resolves the table at 0x8001209c.

meanings.name: EYE_HEIGHT
meanings.evidence: the eye above the feet. camera_pose puts the camera at player_y + bob + crouch - 0x640 (Y points down, so minus is up), and sync_player_pos adds the same 0x640 back when it compares the eye with the three surface planes.

meanings.name: TILE_LOOK_STRIDE
meanings.evidence: 108 bytes to a lighting entry in tile_look, formed as a shift-and-add chain on cell[+9] & 0x3f. 64 entries, reset every frame by light_table_reset from 0x80081c8c.
